title: A Fairer and More Inclusive Singapore for Low-wage Migrant Workers
what_it_is: A Fairer and More Inclusive Singapore for Low-wage Migrant Workers

sections.label: Kickback reports and employers
sections.summary: MOM receives about 960 kickback reports yearly and takes an average of 102 employers to task each year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MOM has said that it receives about 960 reports of kickback offences a year, with an average of 102 employers taken to task each year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon might not feel this is a widespread problem, but if you break it down, that is one employer every three days in Singapore being taken to task for collecting kickbacks from their migrant workers.

sections.label: Migrant workers paying to keep jobs
sections.summary: Migrant workers were asked to pay about $3,000 to continue their employment, more than four times their salary for some.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If any Singaporean were in their shoes, they would be outraged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I recently met some migrant workers who had been asked to pay about $3,000 to be allowed to continue their employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For some, this is more than four times their salary.

sections.label: Kickback reports versus corruption reports
sections.summary: CPIB received 239 corruption reports in 2020, so MOM's 960 kickback reports are more than four times that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To put things in context, CPIB received 239 reports of corruption in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This means MOM's 960 kickback reports are more than four times of all corruption cases in Singapore.

sections.label: Proposed penalty for kickbacks
sections.summary: The speaker proposes raising the maximum sentence to five years' imprisonment and a $100,000 fine, matching bribery penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They should be treated as severely as bribes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I propose that the maximum sentence be raised to five years of imprisonment and a $100,000 fine, matching the maximum penalty for bribery cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

sections.label: SCAL matching migrant workers
sections.summary: Under the scheme, migrant workers who leave their employers get a 30-day window for SCAL to match them to a new employer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under this scheme, migrant workers who leave their employers get a 30-day window in which SCAL will try to match them to a new employer.

sections.label: Dormitory workers unable to walk free
sections.summary: For two years, most of the 300,000 workers living in dormitories have not been able to walk free.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For two years, most of the 300,000 workers living in dormitories have not been able to walk free.

sections.label: Migrant workers COVID-19 symptoms
sections.summary: Last year, 99.9% of COVID-19-infected migrant workers had no or mild symptoms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year, 99.9% of COVID-19-infected migrant workers had either no or mild symptoms.

sections.label: Dormitory residents vaccination rate
sections.summary: 98% of dormitory residents are fully vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Fourth, nearly all of them are fully vaccinated: 98% of dormitory residents are fully vaccinated.

sections.label: Dorm residents community access
sections.summary: On any given day, only about 2% of dorm residents are free to enter the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Three thousand workers on weekdays and 6,000 on weekends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This means on any given day, only about 2% of dorm residents are free to enter the community.

sections.label: 2021 workplace safety statistics
sections.summary: First-half 2021 statistics showed more major injuries and fatalities than 2019 and 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The year 2021 has been an awful year for workplace safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The latest statistics from the first half of 2021 showed a higher level of major injuries and fatalities, compared to 2019 and 2020.

sections.label: Mandatory monthly rest day proposal
sections.summary: The proposed solution is one mandatory monthly rest day for all migrant workers, which they cannot sell back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My proposed solution to this problem is to provide one mandatory rest day a month to all migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Workers should not be allowed to sell these rest days back to their employers; they should be required to rest.

sections.label: Vaccinated residents community entry and rest days
sections.summary: Vaccinated and boosted dormitory residents should be allowed into the community, and migrant workers should get one non-sellable rest day monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Vaccinated and boosted dormitory residents should be allowed to enter the community, subject to all of the intense safe practices and frequent testing that they already face.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, migrant workers should be given at least one rest day every month that they cannot sell back to their employer.

sections.label: EFMA penalties for employers
sections.summary: Under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act, convicted accused persons may face up to two years' imprisonment, a $30,000 fine, or both per charge.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act (EFMA), accused persons, upon conviction, may be sentenced to imprisonment for up to two years or a fine of up to $30,000, or both – per charge.

sections.label: 2018 kickback fine example
sections.summary: In 2018 an employer was fined $120,000 for 10 charges of collecting kickbacks from migrant workers, higher than the $100,000 penalty suggested.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: For instance, in 2018, an employer was fined a total of $120,000 for 10 charges for collecting kickbacks from migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This, in fact, is higher than the $100,000 penalty suggested by the Member.

sections.label: Restitution orders and data analytics
sections.summary: Courts must order offenders to pay a sum equal to benefits deducted or received, and MOM uses data analytics to detect unusual hiring patterns.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: On top of the fines and imprisonment terms meted out, the Courts are also obligated to order the offender to pay a sum which is equal to the amount of the sum or other benefit that the offender had deducted or received.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In recent years, MOM made use of data analytics to identify and detect unusual patterns in hiring practices more quickly and accurately.

sections.label: Mandatory rest day for MDWs
sections.summary: MOM announced implementing by end-2022 at least one rest day per month for migrant domestic workers that cannot be compensated away.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Last year, MOM announced our intention to implement, by end-2022, the requirement for migrant domestic workers to be given at least one rest day per month that cannot be compensated away.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Migrant domestic workers work and live in their employers’ homes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Hence, having a mandatory rest day that cannot be compensated away, will provide migrant domestic workers with mental respite and also more opportunities to form a network of support outside of the households.

sections.label: Rest day work compensation
sections.summary: If work is done on the rest day at the employer's request, the employee must be compensated at twice his regular pay rate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: If work is done on the rest day at the employer's request, the employee must be compensated at twice his regular rate of pay.

sections.label: Vaccinated migrant workers community visits
sections.summary: From 18 December 2021, 3,000 vaccinated migrant workers daily may visit the community on weekdays and 6,000 on weekends and public holidays.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Third, from 18 December 2021, 3,000 vaccinated migrant workers per day are allowed on community visits on weekdays and 6,000 per day on weekends as well as public holidays.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: While the visit slots are not fully utilised even today, we are prepared to adjust the quota to allow even more migrant workers to visit the community as the COVID-19 situation improves further.

sections.label: Kickbacks law, Retention Scheme, court fines
sections.summary: The passage raises a broken kickbacks law, asks about extending the Retention Scheme beyond construction, and says courts should assess maximum fines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: One, we have a piece of legislation, quite a serious one, against kickbacks that is broken once every three days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Two, I understand that the Retention Scheme expires on 28 February.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I think the Senior Minister of State mentioned that they might be extending it a few months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Could I just ask whether that is confirmed just for the construction sector, or are we also going to look into expanding the Retention Scheme to all other sectors, not just the marine and manufacturing?

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But yet, at the same time, that has not been exercised to the maximum.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, I think we should allow the Courts to make the judicial assessment of what the maximum fine should be because there is a lot of headroom for them to use under the current law.
